items.mainDefect: The plural `*_ids` hydration branch calls `obj[k].map` without guarding against a null value, so `foo_ids: null` throws a TypeError.

secondary.defect: The plural branch pushes `undefined` into the hydrated array when a sideloaded record is missing, because it lacks the `if (hydrated)` guard the singular branch has, and consumers then crash.

items.mainDefect: The migration's embed_category lookup indexes `[0]['id']` on a result that can be empty, so it raises and aborts the migration when no matching site_settings row exists.

secondary.defect: The uncategorized_category_id fallback lookup on line 15 can also crash on an empty result, because it indexes `[0]['value']` without a guard.

items.mainDefect: `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError when the embed_category JOIN returns no rows, so the `category_id == 0` fallback never runs and the migration crashes.

secondary.defect: Line 15 can hit the same nil error through `[0]['value']` when the uncategorized_category_id row is missing.

items.mainDefect: `record_for_host` lowercases only the database column and not the referer host, and before_validation never downcases stored hosts, so whether a host matches depends on letter case.

secondary.defect: The validation regex lets a host be stored with a port, but `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host` (no port), so a host saved with a port can never match.

items.mainDefect: The describe string has a typo: 'emeddable' should be 'embeddable'.

secondary.defect: The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the before-block has no effect because `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks EmbeddableHost, so the context name describes the wrong condition.
